questions.question_text: LSAC states that the LSAT is the single best predictor of first-year law school performance. If this claim is true, which of the following must be true?
options: Students with lower LSAT scores will always perform poorly in law school.
The LSAT is the only factor law schools consider during admissions.
Higher LSAT scores correlate more strongly with success in the first year of law school than other individual predictors.
Every student who takes the LSAT will succeed in law school.
questions.explanation: To be the 'single best predictor' means that among all individual indicators used, it provides the most accurate forecast of performance.

questions.question_text: A legal certificate program takes less time and money than a JD degree. Earning a certificate will not allow you to practice law. Based on this, which conclusion is valid?
options: Anyone with a legal certificate is a qualified attorney.
A legal certificate is only useful for people who want to become judges.
An individual aiming to represent clients in court should choose a JD program instead of a legal certificate program.
Legal certificates are the most effective way to become a practicing lawyer.
questions.explanation: Since the text explicitly states that a certificate will not allow you to become an attorney, those seeking to practice law must pursue the JD path.

questions.question_text: LSAC claims the LSAT is the best predictor of first-year law school performance. If this claim is true, what must also be true?
options: All law school applicants will have the same GPA.
High LSAT scores will likely be associated with higher first-year grades.
The LSAT is the only factor law schools use for admissions.
Students with lower LSAT scores will never succeed in law school.
questions.explanation: If the LSAT is a strong predictor of success, it implies a positive correlation between the test score and academic performance in the first year.

questions.question_text: An LSAC Forum starts at 10:00 a.m. Candidates are required to attend a workshop one hour before the forum. At what time must a candidate attend the workshop?
questions.explanation: If the event begins at 10:00 a.m. and the workshop is one hour prior, the candidate must attend at 9:00 a.m.

questions.question_text: To be eligible for the 'Plus, Guided Journey' program, an applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a permanent resident alien, or have DACA status. Which of the following applicants is definitely ineligible?
options: A U.S. citizen applying for law school.
A person with DACA status.
A permanent resident alien with a green card.
A foreign student on a short-term visitor visa with no other listed status.
questions.explanation: The eligibility requirements list specific statuses. A visitor visa is not included in the provided list of criteria.

questions.question_text: A law school is considering implementing an in-house loan program because federal loan limits have decreased. Which of the following arguments best supports this initiative?
options: It will make the law school more expensive for all students.
It helps students continue their education despite changes in federal financial aid.
It will reduce the number of students applying to the school.
It ensures that students no longer need to study for the LSAT.
questions.explanation: The text notes that such programs are a response to federal loan limits, helping applicants who have exhausted federal options.

questions.question_text: An LSAC Forum begins at 10:00 a.m. Attendees must participate in a workshop exactly one hour before the forum starts. At what time must a candidate attend the workshop?
questions.explanation: One hour before 10:00 a.m. is 9:00 a.m.

questions.question_text: To be eligible for the 'Plus, Guided Journey' program, an applicant must be a U.S. citizen, a permanent resident alien, or have DACA status. Which of the following individuals is ineligible?
options: A U.S. citizen
A permanent resident alien
An individual with DACA status
An international student on a short-term visitor visa
questions.explanation: The criteria require status as a citizen, permanent resident, or DACA recipient; a short-term visitor visa does not meet these specific requirements.

questions.question_text: A student must attend exactly three of four available workshops: Ethics, Admissions, Financing, and Diversity. If the student attends Financing, they cannot attend Diversity. Which set of workshops could the student attend?
options: Financing, Diversity, Ethics
Ethics, Admissions, Diversity
Financing, Admissions, Diversity
Financing, Admissions, Ethics
questions.explanation: The rule states if Financing is chosen, Diversity cannot be chosen. Option 2 does not include Financing, so both Ethics, Admissions, and Diversity are valid.

questions.question_text: Three candidates are applying for a scholarship. Candidate X has a higher LSAT score than Y. Candidate Z has a lower score than X but a higher score than Y. Who has the lowest score?
options: Candidate X
Candidate Y
Candidate Z
Not enough information
questions.explanation: X > Y and X > Z > Y. Therefore, Y has the lowest score.

questions.question_text: A law school is considering an in-house loan program because federal loan limits dropped. Which argument best supports this initiative?
options: The school has extra office space for loan processing
The school wants to increase the number of total applicants
The loans help applicants who have exhausted federal funding continue their education
The school wants to make a profit from interest rates
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states the program is a response to help applicants who have exhausted federal options.
